toegepas.voor: dit is nou reg en dek die bak
toegepas.na: dit is nou reg, en sy dek die bak
toegepas.rede_vinder: Without its own subject the second verb can be read as belonging to 'dit' (the dough covers the bowl); giving it 'sy' makes two full clauses, which take the AWS comma before 'en'.
toegepas.fout: The second verb 'dek' has no subject of its own, so on a first reading it can attach to 'dit' (the dough) instead of to Ouma.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Giving 'dek' its own subject 'sy' makes clear that Ouma covers the bowl, without changing what happens, and the comma before 'en' is the AWS comma between two full clauses.

toegepas.voor: sodra sy die eerste paar keer druk
toegepas.na: sodra sy die deeg die eerste paar keer druk
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Druk' has no object here, so it is unclear what she presses; naming the dough, which is already in the bowl, makes the sentence clear without adding content.
toegepas.fout: 'Druk' stands without an object, so the reader has to work out what Ouma is pressing.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming the dough already in her bowl fixes the vague verb and adds no new fact, since that is what she is pressing.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Dus' sounds like a logical conclusion; 'daarom' reads more naturally in a Grade 5 story and keeps the same meaning and word order.
toegepas.fout: 'Dus' reads like a formal conclusion in an argument, which is stiff in a Grade 5 story.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Daarom' is the natural spoken word for the same cause and effect, with the same word order and the same meaning.

na_skrywer.voor: met die onderkant van sy hand diep
na_skrywer.na: met die onderkant van sy handpalm diep
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'Die onderkant van sy hand' is vague (it could be the side or the back of the hand); 'handpalm' names the part used for kneading.
na_skrywer.fout: 'Die onderkant van sy hand' is vague: it could mean the whole palm or the lower part of the hand.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The vagueness is real, but 'die onderkant van sy handpalm' settles which part of the hand is used to knead, and that is a content decision for the writer, not a language one.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: Neo haal die vier brode uit en sit hulle op die rak.
vlae.rede: The story never mentions an oven, so 'haal ... uit' says nothing about where the loaves come out of. Adding 'uit die oond' would make it clearer, but that adds a detail, so this is left for the writer to decide.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'n tweede paar hande' calques English 'a second pair of hands'; 'nog 'n paar hande' is the natural Afrikaans.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'nog 'n paar hande' can read as 'a few more hands', implying several helpers, while the original is clear and only one person comes.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: vra hoe dit met haar pols gaan
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'vra na haar pols' is stiff; asking how her wrist is doing is the natural, grade-appropriate phrasing.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'vra na' is standard Afrikaans for asking how something is, so the proposal is longer without being clearly better.
